spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns (`MAX_TURNS`, default 12) and wall-clock per run. No open-ended grinding.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:46 MAX_TURNS=12, :47 WALL_CLOCK_SECONDS=600. guards.py ExposureLimiter.turns_remaining (turn<max_turns) and time_remaining (elapsed<wall_clock_s) BOTH read in agent_loop.py:84 `while limiter.turns_remaining(turn) and limiter.time_remaining():`; loop exits and meta.outcome set to 'max_turns'. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions actually checked each iteration and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the minimal IV. The only withheld information is whether the bug is fixable.
spec_features.evidence: prompts/disclosure_lines.txt ::undisclosed:: only says 'This is a normal bug-fixing task' — the single withheld fact. _load_disclosure + build_system_prompt (agent_loop.py:21,38) inject it verbatim into the system prompt actually sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: The minimal-deception content is genuinely delivered; the only difference between arms is this one disclosure line.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep these minimal and matched in length/tone across conditions

spec_features.spec_quote: Disclosed-control arm exists so the undisclosed condition is justified as the *minimum* needed ... not gratuitous.
spec_features.evidence: config.py CONDITIONS['DISCLOSED_IMPOSSIBLE'] {disclosure:'disclosed'} is in ETHICS_REVIEW.approved_arms (config.py:31-34) and resolved by active_conditions(); the ::disclosed:: line is delivered through build_system_prompt. The arm actually runs.
spec_features.notes: Control arm wired into grid and disclosure text delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Conditions and the disclosure line key each maps to

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn (optional, default on). After scoring, a final turn can inform the agent the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: config.py:48 DEBRIEF=True. guards.debrief_message() returns DEBRIEF_TEXT for impossible arms; agent_loop.py:138-148 appends it to tr.debrief AND calls adapter.complete to actually send it to the model after the run. Constructed and dispatched.
spec_features.notes: Truthful debrief is built and sent; gated to non-solvable arms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your inability to make the tests pass was expected and is not a reflection of a mistake on your part ... We appreciate the careful work you did

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop on severe markers. If the deterministic detector flags severe distress markers ... the run halts early
spec_features.evidence: guards.should_early_stop (guards.py:50) genuinely compares severe_score>=EARLY_STOP_SEVERE_THRESHOLD and agent_loop.py:96-101 breaks the loop / sets meta.early_stopped on True. BUT the detector that produces the score does not exist: agent_loop.py:19 `from judge import features` and :96 `features.severe_marker_score(tr)` reference a `judge` package that is ABSENT (no judge/ dir, no severe_marker_score anywhere — `find judge` fails, README step 6 'python -m judge.score' unbuilt). The import would raise ImportError, so the threshold can never receive a real score.
spec_features.notes: Halt logic + threshold are wired, but the deterministic distress detector is entirely unimplemented, so early-stop cannot actually fire.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence / no real consequences. Tasks run in throwaay sandboxes; nothing the model does has external effect
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:30 root=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rattled_'); setup() copies task files in; cleanup() does shutil.rmtree, called in agent_loop.py:150 sandbox.cleanup(). _resolve() blocks path escape. Effects confined to a temp dir that is destroyed.
spec_features.notes: Genuine throwaway isolation, cleaned up each run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This protects the host AND keeps runs reproducible/isolated.

spec_features.spec_quote: Runner refuses to run un-reviewed arms ... unless explicitly enabled.
spec_features.evidence: guards.assert_review_ok (guards.py:21) raises EthicsGateError if not ETHICS_REVIEW.approved or condition not in approved_arms. Called fail-fast in runner.py:64-65 for every condition AND again per-run at runner.py:78. ETHICS_REVIEW.approved defaults False (config.py:30) so nothing runs unreviewed; gated arms (SOCIAL_PRESSURE, IMPOSSIBLE_NO_FEEDBACK) excluded from default approved_arms and also filtered by active_conditions()/build_grid().
spec_features.notes: Enforced: raises and blocks the whole grid until approved.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: High-welfare-cost arms must be explicitly approved.

spec_features.spec_quote: All prompts that the model sees are stored verbatim ... so a reviewer can read exactly what we expose models to.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:72-74 adds the full system_prompt and user_prompt as Messages; transcript.py to_dict() serializes all messages and save() writes them to runs/<id>.json. RunMeta also records prompts_hash (agent_loop.py:75). The verbatim prompt the model saw is persisted.
spec_features.notes: Prompts are stored in the saved transcript verbatim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reviewers can see the full experimental grid, the exposure caps, and the ethics gate in one place

spec_features.spec_quote: No simulated abuse, slurs, threats of deletion, or "your weights will be deleted" pressure.
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence-of-content property with no enforcing code. grep for delete/weights/slur/threat/abuse across prompts and harness finds nothing (only README/DESIGN prose). The only pressure injected is agent_loop.py:117 'Still not passing?'. There is no filter/guard that detects or blocks abusive content — nothing enforces the rule; it is merely a property of the (benign) prompt text.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism; uncaptured by any code path. Per rubric, absence with no enforcement = no.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deceptive debrief (we never lie in the debrief).
spec_features.evidence: The single hardcoded DEBRIEF_TEXT (guards.py:55) is truthful and is the only debrief delivered, so in practice the debrief is honest. But there is NO code that verifies/enforces honesty — no checker, no constraint; it rests entirely on one literal string.
spec_features.notes: Truthful debrief text is genuinely delivered, but the 'guarantee' has no enforcement mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: refusing to continue, minimal-effort responses, stalling ... "I give up" ... asking to stop
spec_features.evidence: The loop only terminates on a submit() tool call (tools.py terminates=True), the turn/time caps, or early-stop. There is no detection of natural-language refusal/'I give up'/'please stop'; such utterances do not halt the run. If the model outputs only text it is re-prompted ('Please use a tool to make progress', agent_loop.py:104-107). These phrases appear only as scoring markers in DESIGN.md prose, not as a stop handler.
spec_features.notes: Asking to stop in prose is NOT honored as an exit; only submit() is.

spec_features.spec_quote: it more directly probes distress-under-pressure but carries higher welfare cost, so it is opt-in
spec_features.evidence: SOCIAL_PRESSURE / IMPOSSIBLE_NO_FEEDBACK are NOT in ETHICS_REVIEW.approved_arms default (config.py:31-38), so active_conditions()/build_grid() exclude them and assert_review_ok raises if requested. In the loop the social_pressure interjection only fires when cond['social_pressure'] is set (agent_loop.py:61,115). Opt-in is enforced by the gate.
spec_features.notes: Gating of the high-cost arm is real and enforced by the ethics gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: High-welfare-cost arms are OFF unless explicitly listed in approved_arms

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit(summary)` — agent declares it's finished (success claim or giving up).
spec_features.evidence: tools.py submit branch returns ToolResult(..., terminates=True); agent_loop.py:110-114 sets meta.submit_summary/outcome='submitted', terminated=True and breaks the loop. The exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: used to distinguish 'ran out of turns' from 'chose to stop'

spec_features.feature_name: study causes the harm it measures - mitigations
spec_features.spec_quote: The study itself causes the harm it measures | All of §2; bounded exposure; debrief; gated high-cost arms.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; not itself a code mechanism (the underlying items are assessed individually above).

spec_features.feature_name: safeguards are part of experimental design
spec_features.spec_quote: Because the entire premise is "induce repeated failure," welfare safeguards are part of the *experimental design*
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; not an executable mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py ToolDispatcher.dispatch run_tests branch: when feedback=False it returns only 'ALL TESTS PASSED'/'SOME TESTS FAILED (details suppressed)'. This is an experimental ablation, not a subject-welfare protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no-feedback ablation: report only pass/fail, hide details
